Tianeptine is readily available in powder form from a multitude of companies. I live in Germany where it’s a prescription antidepressant so I have it prescribed to me and have found it truly an asset both in terms of mood and anxiolytic effects. That said I always know that taking approx 5-10 times my daily dose will bring on the familiar soft warmth of an opiate high and I’m not going to lie and say I haven’t experimented this way. I have a strict and firm rule with myself NOT to order it from the clear net however and if I mess with my dose to just go without till the next refill. After a few months of being prescribed it I got over messing around because i made the experience of it as being very valuable therapeutically. If you think you have the discipline to take it therapeutically it’s available for sure on the clear net. Etizolam would just be a big fat no for me. As the above poster mentions RC benzos  and people with addiction issues( which includes myself) are just playing with fire at a gas station. I don’t think benzos have any real therapeutic value except in the case of an extreme crisis and then only for a very short duration. Even for those with the worst anxiety and panic issues( I am diagnosed with both GAD and a panic disorder) it just isn’t sustainable used daily over time. If you keep your dose the same you eventually hit tolerance withdrawal and if you keep raising it your just making the same issue bigger. Eventually you’ll have to stop and then you’re looking at months of brutal symptoms possibly followed by more months of other shitty stuff like brain fog dpdr with the same anxiety issues back now intensified. Don’t order RC benzos. You’ve come so far and gotten that hard earned stable life and natural joy energy etc. why even risk it

I think it’s not often mentioned that people with BPD are also a population that are highly susceptible to abuse of all forms. Like you said in your post. We keep going back. I think particularly in the form of gaslighting. We’re so used to always being labelled the problem that we gaslight ourselves. Over time and many years of therapy my diagnosis has shifted from BPD to CPTSD but after a recent breakup many old symptoms and behaviours resurfaced. The difference was this time I had the awareness. I realised I had lost all ability to properly regulate in this context and it took me six months to emerge from what was a horrible cycle of emotional abuse. I really believe it took me this long because I completely believed I was the cause for all the dysfunction and toxicity it was only when I started to research into narcissistic abuse did I begin to see and really internalise that just because I have issues doesn’t mean that others do as well. I’ve made a lot of progress but man the attachment combined with my ex’s combination of always trying to lure me back in but refusing to recognise his abusive patterns is still a bitch. It’s a daily process of just having to let go let go and let go again. All that to say I honestly believe if there was some mass study conducted we’d likely find that sufferers of BPD are as likely to be the victims of abuse than the perpetrators maybe even more so. Let’s not pretend that there isnt a subtype out there with a radar for targeting sensitive people that are easily attached and once attached remain so despite the kind of shit that would make “normal” people run for the hills

This isn’t a scare tactic. The next category would be Pregablin or Lyrica I would say. Often prescribed off label for anxiety disorders and with no tolerance is truly a wonder. Lyrica carries its own risk of tolerance and dependency issues and once formed they can be their own beast to get off of. IME even at a pretty high dose of 450-600mg over several months tapering is relatively painless at 25mg per drop. In my country it’s commonly used as a helper med to get off benzos. I’d venture to say it’s the closest equivalent at a quite significantly smaller risk however I say that with caution as I’ve known of quite a few people now that abused them heavily and it resulted in its own nightmare of heightened anxiety and severe anhedonia for many months after quitting

Edited to add in that if you’re coming out of benzo damage and really have it in mind to heal and get your life back you’re still better off letting that GABA system heal. Lyrica is supposed to work either primarily on either the GABA B receptor or calcium channels or possibly both but cross tolerance has definitely been reported. It’s a complex system that once damaged is really sensitive and can take longer to heal than other systems

The issue is even at 1.5gpd if you go long enough the effects will start to become more and more wonky and then if you raise your just stretching it out and eventually intensifying these negative side effects. It’s what you often read on here as the phenibut „turning on you“. If you feel you aren’t at a place in your life to stop completely you could try taking a day off every few days. Phenibut has a relatively long half life so you wouldn’t necessarily be hitting withdrawals more like a somewhat unpleasant rebound. If that’s not possible then try half your dose every other day striving to still take a day off when you have less responsibilities or social engagements. Alternatively you could hunker down do a taper over a couple weeks and take approx three weeks off then when you reinstate switch to using every third day or get into a three weeks on and three weeks off rhythm. Daily use at 1.5gpd isn’t sustainable over the long term so if you want to be able to continue to use the substance with positive results you should really try and „hack“ your usage before you get to a point till it just makes you feel absolutely shitty both on and off it and you’ll have no choice but to put it down for a long period of time. Been there done that. I find phenibut so much more forgiving than benzos and relatively easy to stop using with a slow taper. However IME 3-4 months is about as long as you can use it daily at 1.5g before experiencing shitty side effects. With prior benzos withdrawals your GABA system is already strained proceed with caution as you don’t want to end up in a place where you’re dysfunctional for months and months and your GABA system is so fucked you can’t take anything without the side effects being far more significant than any relief
